old_caption: The video showcases a close-up view of a rotating propeller, likely from an aircraft or helicopter. The propeller blades are metallic gray with black speckles, indicating wear or dirt accumulation. The central hub is also metallic gray, with visible signs of wear and some dark spots. The background is blurred, suggesting a shallow depth of field. The propeller spins, causing the blades to blur and the viewing angle to shift relative to the hub. The lighting is bright, casting reflections on the metallic surfaces. There are no other objects, characters, or animals present in the frame, focusing entirely on the propeller and its rotation.
original_wisa_caption: The video showcases a close-up view of a spinning propeller, likely from an aircraft or helicopter. The propeller blades are metallic gray with black speckles, indicating wear or dirt accumulation. The central hub is also metallic gray, with visible signs of wear and some dark spots. The background is blurred, suggesting a fast-moving scene, possibly during flight. The propeller rotates rapidly, creating a blur effect on the blades, emphasizing their speed. The lighting is bright, casting reflections on the metallic surfaces, which enhances the dynamic motion of the propeller. There are no other objects, characters, or animals present in the frame, focusing entirely on the spinning propeller and its movement. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, maintaining a consistent angle that captures the detailed motion of the propeller.
caption: The video showcases a tight close-up of an aircraft propeller, its dark glossy spinner cone marked with small specks and a diagonal light streak, surrounded by long blades tipped in yellow and gold against a heavily blurred cityscape of tall buildings. Throughout the excerpt the blade cluster drifts steadily in orientation, the left and right blades rising toward horizontal-up while the upper blade leans further right. The whole assembly thus appears to turn slowly. The blades remain sharply defined with no motion-blur disc, indicating a slow spin. As the view progresses the framing tightens on the hub, the spinner cone occupying more of the image while the blades look thinner and more edge-on. The dark lower air-intake opening with its pale yellow rim becomes progressively more visible. The blurred background slides and brightens, the right side washing out toward white. This suggests camera movement alongside the apparent rotation.

necessarily a complete action and it is NOT a loop. Describe the visible portion of a process
without inventing how it began or how it ultimately ends. A process may already be happening
on the first frame and still be happening after the last. Do not force the endpoints to match,
infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
